brief_context: Monastic ruins mentioned as a local attraction.

In one of these gardens stand the monastic ruins of Torre Abbey which was founded by one of the courtiers of Richard Coeur de Lion. One of the buildings is known as The Spanish Barn because the crew of a vessel of the Spanish Armada was imprisoned in it.

brief_context: House built by Isaac Merritt Singer.
brief_extract: Close to the church is the family house of the Kirkhams which is an interesting example of early domestic architecture. But perhaps the most fascinating house in the town is Oldway which was built in 1874 by Isaac Merritt Singer, the inventor and manufacturer of the sewing machine, whose name has become a household word with women all over the world. Unfortunately, this rich American did not live long to enjoy his Devon palace with its replicas of rooms at Versailles and its Italian gardens for he died one year after its completion, but his house now the property of the town is a lasting memorial to him.

A. MAY, Magazine Secretary, Glasgow

brief_context: Geographic context for the size of the power station.
article_title: VISIT TO LONGANNET POWER STATION, KINCARDINE
brief_extract: Longannet Power Station, which has an installed capacity of 2,400 megawatts, is the largest single under-taking in the Board's present building programme and the biggest engineering project ever to be carried out in Scotland. It is also the first of its size to be commissioned in Europe, the power obtained from four 6,000 megawatt units, the boilers and turbo-generators being greater and larger than any previously ordered for a European power station. In addition to the economics affected by choosing a suitable site, both running and capital costs have been kept to a minimum by obtaining the required station output from four identical high-capacity units which operate at advanced steam conditions to give an overall station efficiency of over 39%.

brief_context: Used as a size comparison for microwave waveguides.
brief_extract: At microwave frequencies, the energy is sent down metal pipes or tubes, known as waveguides, and the longer the wavelength of the energy the larger the tube required. To send television signals or vhf radio waves down a metal tube would need a tube the size of the London Underground. Even for microwaves at the longer wavelengths, say 30 cm, the tube would be 10" x 5" in cross section, and it is more common and more economical to use coaxial line at these wavelengths.

brief_context: The location where the author grows strawberries and tests mowers.
brief_extract:
Strawberries
You have probably been eating strawberries for the last month, particularly if a row had been cloched up in early February and a little bottom heat provided by soil warming wires. At the Electric Garden, Syon Park, we grow five rows of Hummi Grande, one covered with glass cloches, one with polythene, both over low voltage soil warming wires; then two more rows, one glass cloched and one plastic with no soil warming and finally a row without any protection at all. We have been picking large luscious berries for over a month now and expect the plants will keep on bearing fruit at least until mid-July.

article_title: VISIT TO THE G.P.O. RADIO TOWER, BIRMINGHAM
brief_extract:
RADIO TOWER, BIRMINGHAM
by MRS. GANE, Magazine Secretary, Halesowen
The purpose of the 498 ft Radio Tower, situated in the centre of Birmingham, is to form a main link in the chain of microwave communications between London and most cities and towns throughout the country. brief_extract: What about the hardness of water? In London, for instance, the water is very hard whereas in other parts of the country the water is soft. How do you deal with this internationally?

brief_extract: Q. Am I not right in thinking that in the USA it is quite usual for water softeners to be installed in homes in hard water areas? A.

There is greater similarity between the sizes of plates used in British and American households than in British households compared with those in France and other Continental countries. Q.

brief_extract: I think the height of the trees in relation to their girth. brief_extract: A. At the Hilton Hotel where we all stayed, the cuisine was international. At a nearby self-service café where we mostly had breakfast, there were additions to the standard breakfast such as a type of pancake, and a hot bun which was a cross between a muffin and a queencake.

brief_extract: Generally helpings were larger than in an English restaurant and a standard steak would be almost hanging over the edge of the plate. LIBRARY

MEMBERS of the London Branch recently visited the BP Plastics Division at
Burgh Heath to see their 'Plastics House'. This was very much of an experimental project
and will not be a commercial proposition for
many years to come, largely because most of the
materials used are manufactured only on the
Continent at present and also because of the
opposition of the conventional builder and the
Building Societies to this revolutionary idea of
building.

brief_extract: At Ffestiniog, one of the hydro-electric power stations in North Wales, the Generating Board undertook to face the power station with local stone. The type of stone preferred was that which had been used for many imposing buildings in the Vale of Ffestiniog but its source was elusive. After considerable detective work, involving questioning of a number of retired quarrymen, one of the original quarries, long disused, was located and stone obtained.

brief_context: Location of a historic castle mentioned for comparison.
brief_extract: After considerable detective work, involving questioning of a number of retired quarrymen, one of the original quarries, long disused, was located and stone obtained. As a result, Ffestiniog power station is probably the largest building to be built largely of local stone in North Wales since the Castles of Harlech and Criccieth were built in Norman times, 800-900 years ago. Nature trails have been established in the grounds of several power stations and, at Dungeness in Kent, where a nuclear power station is operating and another one is under construction, the Generating Board assist in the preservation of a bird sanctuary and insect colony.

booklet competition on an electrical theme for affiliated schools. Solihull Branch were proud that a girl from an affiliated school
was a winner in the Midlands Poster Competition.

brief_context: Institution involved in a joint project on noise levels.
brief_extract:
Enquiries
Enquiries on cooking equipment were the most numerous, followed closely by enquiries on refrigerators and home freezers, with interest in laundry equipment a little way behind. An interesting discussion on noise levels in electrical equipment took place between the Home Economics Department and a student engaged in a project undertaken jointly by Belling & Co Ltd and Enfield College of Technology. The public has come to accept the advantages of automation in the home as commonplace, but even greater expectations are cherished by the lady who wanted a floor polisher that would scrub, rinse and dry the floors and by another enquirer who was looking for an electronic housemaid 'because a good daily help is so hard to come by'.

brief_extract:
School News

The winner, Christine Armstrong (centre), with Susan Knight (highly commended), and Miss P. Penn, Aylesbury Branch Chairman at the presentation of prizes to Aylesbury schoolgirls. (Bucks Herald)

Home Planning Project for Aylesbury Schoolgirls

In pursuance of the Home Planning Campaign Aylesbury EAW Branch devised a Home Planning project for the girls of Grange County Secondary Modern School which is affiliated to the Branch.

location_standardised: London, Greater London, England, United Kingdom
brief_context: Location of the Design Centre visited by the students.
article_title: Home Planning Project for Aylesbury Schoolgirls
brief_extract: Four girls undertook the project which was to design an average 3-bedroomed house paying particular attention to the placing and number of power points, work top heights, general lay-out of the kitchen and a special feature that would be included in homes of the future. The project took one year to complete and arrangements were made for the girls to visit the Design Centre in London, a local building site, Electricity Showrooms, the Borough Architect's Department and local furnishers in order to gain ideas on colour in the home. article_title: The Priorities of Women in the '70s
brief_extract:
Technical barriers can be removed through harmonisation of national standards, enabling exporters to work to the same standards for both home and overseas markets. This was a main factor in the UK decision to change to the metric system. Increased Activity
Standardisation work has to keep pace with rapid technological developments.

brief_context: Reference to the 1790 invitation to join the metric system.
brief_extract:
Since the 18th century
The metric system has evolved since the 18th century, and different countries adopted different practices and all retained some elements of their pre-metric systems of measurements. The argument about going metric has been going on in this country since 1790 when the French invited us to join them in getting the metric system going, and for more than 100 years we have been signatories of the Metric Convention. Since 1897 the use of metric measures has been legal in this country for all but a limited number of purposes.

brief_context: Mentioned regarding industrial stock levels compared to British industry.
brief_extract: Reduction of inventory, simplification of all ordering and all accounting for these fundamental stock items will be of real and lasting benefit to our industries. The value of stock in hand and work in progress in British industry is about twice as much as is tied up in that way in USA, and if in the course of metrication we can achieve a 10 per cent reduction in variety we shall release a sum bigger than the country's total gold and convertible currency reserves. Some companies have seized the opportunity to incorporate in their metric designs numerous improvements which might possibly have been ignored but for the stimulus offered by metrication.

Members visited the station where it was pointed out that the accurate measurement of the energy supplied to each consumer was an essential requirement in the distribution of electricity. This new station caters for all the Board's meter testing requirements and also provides facilities for general testing of electrical equipment and for applied research.

location_standardised: Newcastle-upon-Tyne, Tyne and Wear, England, United Kingdom
brief_context: Collaborating institution for the research station's design and studies.
article_title: VISIT TO NEEB'S TESTING AND RESEARCH STATION
brief_extract: The brief called for very little dust, a narrow range of ambient temperature, and a good level of illumination. The research carried out by a large number of organisations into the thermal environment of buildings included studies by the Building Research Station, the Heating and Ventilating Research Association and the Department of Building Science of the School of Architecture at the University of Newcastle upon Tyne. A specialist group was set up consisting of the Electricity Council, NEEB and Newcastle University.
